name: Storing & Prepping Produce
summary: What goes in the fridge and what stays on the counter, keeping herbs and greens fresh, and washing produce.

rows: Leafy greens, broccoli, cauliflower, carrots, celery, peppers, zucchini, cucumbers, green beans, mushrooms (in a paper bag), berries, grapes, apples, citrus
Tomatoes, bananas, avocados, stone fruit and pears until ripe (then the fridge), whole melons
Potatoes, sweet potatoes, onions, garlic, winter squash. Keep potatoes and onions apart: onions make potatoes sprout.

blocks.text: Bananas, avocados, apples and tomatoes give off ethylene gas, which ripens other produce faster. Ripen an avocado quicker in a paper bag with a banana; keep them away from greens you want to last.

items: **Soft herbs** (parsley, cilantro, mint, dill): trim the stems and stand them in a glass of water in the fridge, loosely covered with a bag. Basil stays on the counter in water; the fridge blackens it.
**Woody herbs** (rosemary, thyme, sage): wrap in a barely damp paper towel in a bag or container in the fridge.
**Salad greens**: wash, dry very well (a salad spinner helps), and store in a container lined with paper towels.

sections.heading: Washing
blocks: Rinse produce under running water just before you use it, not before storing (moisture speeds spoiling). Rub firm produce with your hands or a brush. Soap and produce washes aren't needed. Wash even things you'll peel, like melons and avocados, since the knife carries dirt from the skin into the flesh. Bagged greens labeled "pre-washed" don't need washing again.
